concerns.message: Item 8 says the test "taps E" after the hint appears, and "creeps in with short throttle taps". The sea keyboard can't register a quick tap. `KeyboardHelm` only tracks which keys are currently held (apps/web/src/keyboard.ts:47), and the page reads it every 16.7 ms on a setInterval (apps/web/src/main.ts:12,141). Playwright's `keyboard.press` sends keydown and keyup back to back, so the read often falls outside the press. The server holds on to a button until the next world step (apps/server/src/inputGate.ts:66-90), but only after the client has sent it. The duel keyboard does record taps (`tapped` in duelKeyboard.ts:46); the sea keyboard doesn't. Throttle taps have a similar problem: under load, `waitForTimeout` can stretch a 100 ms tap into many 50 ms world steps, so how much a tap speeds the ship up is unpredictable.
concerns.consequence: The fix for the flaky test brings in a new flake. An E tap that gets dropped leaves `hud-dock` at "at sea" until the test times out. The test can pass 5 local repeats on a quiet machine and still fail under the verifier's load, which is the failure this item exists to remove. The acceptance should say "hold E until the HUD shows the dock". That is safe with no throttle held, and docking with interact held is an existing tested rule. Otherwise the sea keyboard should record taps the way the duel keyboard does, with a unit test.

concerns.message: The hub check passes a route if it comes within SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES (10) of the hub. The claim that "ships crossing between any two islands can see each other there" doesn't follow. Two routes passing on opposite sides of the hub can be 20 tiles apart, twice the sight radius.
concerns.consequence: The validator can pass a map where the four routes never come within sight of each other, so "ships meet" is still a hope. A radius of SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES/2 makes the stated guarantee true at the same cost.

concerns.message: "Every shortest sea route between neighbouring islands" is ambiguous in two ways. The existing validator's idea of neighbour is `nearestIsland`, which gives one pair per island (seaValidation.ts:198). In a 2×2 layout that leaves one orthogonal pair per island unchecked, and the other docks on each island aren't covered either. Separately, octile Dijkstra produces many equal-cost paths. If the worker rebuilds one path from predecessors, the check only proves that some shortest path passes the hub, not every one.
concerns.consequence: An edge route that the shoal bars leave open, from an unchecked dock pair or island pair or along a tied path, can pass validation. The validator then wrongly reports that traffic is funnelled. The exact check is cheap: for all island pairs and all dock pairs, run Dijkstra with the hub disc blocked and require the cost to rise, or the target to become unreachable.

concerns.message: The browser helpers hard-code today's numbers. They use 16 px (tests/e2e/helpers.ts:7). `sailTo` wants speeds between 14 and 64 and brakes above the wanted speed + 8 (helpers.ts:258-261). `sailTo` also steers in a straight line with no pathfinding, and the web unit test clamps the camera at 224 × 208 (web.test.ts:159). On a map where every tile is within 10 tiles of an obstacle, straight legs between waypoints will often cross shoals.
concerns.consequence: Pixel and minimap checks sample the wrong pixels. Also, `sailTo` asks for a speed of 64 that the ship can never reach at 39 max, and ships run aground on legs between waypoints and stall until the 30 s timeout in two-ships-sync, out-of-sight and sail-and-dock. The worker should take these numbers from TILE_PIXELS and shipTuning, and check each test waypoint pair for a clear straight line against the map.

concerns.message: Decisions let the worker rescale the dock reach along with speed. At 39/64 of 384, the reach becomes about 234 sub-units, under one tile. That shrinks the zone where the "Press E to dock" hint shows, and item 8's creep approach depends on that zone. The out-of-sight test also needs a clear straight row of about 16 tiles with room to turn (turning radius about 1.6 tiles). The row must be at least 12 tiles from the top and bottom edges and at least 17 from the sides, so the camera isn't clamped. The density rule makes such rows scarce.
concerns.consequence: A dock reach under one tile makes the "Press E" window short, so it can pass during HUD lag and the creep approach fails more often. Keep the reach at 384 or more: it doesn't depend on speed. If the out-of-sight row is left until the tests are written, the map may have to be redrawn after it has passed the validators. Plan the row into the sketch, for example anchored to the hub.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: For sail-and-dock, drive the ship into the dock instead of creeping in with taps. Make the last waypoint a few tiles out on the dock's axis (for the south dock, `dock.tileX, dock.tileY + 3`). At low speed, turn until the HUD heading is exactly 48, then hold ahead and E together. The shore stops the ship at speed 0 inside the dock reach and it moors. simulation.test.ts:393 already unit-tests this rule, and it doesn't depend on timing under load. So there are no taps, and no key releases timed to the hint. The same idea works for the hub: build the funnel into the layout. Put shoal walls on the map's midlines with gaps only inside the hub disc. Then validate it by blocking the disc in Dijkstra, rather than by rebuilding one shortest path.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: This takes about 10 minutes on the base commit. In a scratch Playwright test, place a ship at rest on the tile just south of Palm Key's south dock, facing north. Run 20 cycles: `page.keyboard.press("KeyE")`, wait up to 2 s for `hud-dock` to show the dock, then cast off with a brief ArrowDown and wait for \"at sea\". Count the moorings. Repeat with a 150 ms down/up. If `press()` misses more than a few, item 8 must say to hold E, or `KeyboardHelm` must record taps, before any worker starts. Running the same test with `--workers=4 --repeat-each=10` shows how much load makes the miss rate worse.
